That doesn't leave much room once you add the selenium you get from food. / An umbrella review of meta-analyses found routine supplementation isn't recommended once a deficiency is fixed. Most of the positive observational findings were rated low quality. / The same review flagged higher selenium intake as a possible risk factor for type 2 diabetes and skin cancer. Too much also causes selenosis, which means hair loss, brittle nails and stomach upset.
Where you can get it: Sold across the US on its own or inside multivitamins.
Study: Selenium intake and multiple health-related outcomes: an umbrella review of meta-analyses

What it is for: Herbal sleep aid taken before bed for occasional trouble sleeping.
Keep an eye on: A pooled analysis of 16 trials found a small edge over placebo when people were asked if their sleep improved. But the authors saw signs of publication bias and said most of the trials were poorly designed. / Doses, extracts and how long people took it vary a lot between studies, so nobody knows which product or dose works. / Even the skeptical reviews found a good safety record, with side effects no worse than placebo in most trials.
Where you can get it: Sold across the US as capsules, tablets, tea and tinctures. The strength varies a lot by brand.
Study: Valerian for sleep: a systematic review and meta-analysis

What it is for: Herbal supplement marketed for stress and anxiety, usually sold as a standardized root extract.
Keep an eye on: The main trial behind the stress claim was one study of 64 people over 60 days using one company's extract. Stress scores and cortisol did drop significantly, but it was a small trial of a single product. / StatPearls doesn't have an article on ashwagandha yet. Its general guidance on herbal anxiety remedies says the evidence for the whole group is limited and not all of them are safe, with kava and St. John's wort as the examples. / Side effects in the trial were mild and about the same as placebo, but case reports have linked ashwagandha to rare liver injury, so it isn't risk-free.
Where you can get it: Sold across the US under many extract names (KSM-66, Sensoril and others). They're standardized differently, so the doses aren't interchangeable.
Study: A prospective, randomized double-blind, placebo-controlled study of safety and efficacy of a high-concentration full-spectrum extract of ashwagandha root in reducing stress and anxiety in adults

What it is for: Three-ingredient tablet for period cramps, bloating and irritability. It has a pain reliever, a stimulant and a mild antihistamine.
Keep an eye on: The closest trial used a different third ingredient (pamabrom instead of pyrilamine) and found it worked about as well as a naproxen product. That's encouraging, but it didn't test this exact formula. / The usual acetaminophen liver rules apply, and it's easy to take it with another pain reliever or cold medicine in the same week without realizing it. / Pyrilamine is a sedating first-generation antihistamine, so don't take it before driving or with alcohol.
Where you can get it: Sold across the US. Midol also sells versions without the antihistamine and versions with naproxen under the same brand, so check which one you're buying.
Study: Naproxen, paracetamol and pamabrom versus paracetamol, pyrilamine and pamabrom in primary dysmenorrhea: a randomized, double-blind clinical trial

What it is for: Benadryl's sedating antihistamine plus pseudoephedrine for allergy symptoms with nasal congestion.
Keep an eye on: Diphenhydramine is on the Beers Criteria list of drugs older adults should usually avoid. It's linked to next-day grogginess, confusion and anticholinergic side effects, and adding a decongestant doesn't change that. / Pseudoephedrine reliably raises blood pressure and heart rate, even in people whose high blood pressure is under control, and this immediate-release 60 mg dose causes a bigger jump than extended-release forms. / It's kept behind the pharmacy counter, with ID and purchase limits, because pseudoephedrine is used to make meth illegally.
Where you can get it: Behind the counter across the US. For daytime, a non-drowsy combo like Claritin-D, Allegra-D or Zyrtec-D is usually a better pick.
Study: Effect of oral pseudoephedrine on blood pressure and heart rate: a meta-analysis
